smell_elimination.justification: The refactoring moves the feature envy code from BlockReference to Context, but doesn't eliminate it. The same problematic patterns (self.eval_ctx.output_coerce_mode, self.environment.get_block_output_processor) remain, just relocated. Environment.get_block_output_processor and the registry infrastructure are untouched, leaving the core smell artifacts in place.

cross_file_coordination.justification: Only runtime.py is modified. The Environment.get_block_output_processor method in environment.py, the utils.py registry (_block_render_registry, get_block_renderer), and EvalContext.output_coerce_mode in nodes.py are all left completely unchanged. This leaves significant orphaned infrastructure that was introduced specifically for the smell.

structural_soundness.justification: Introduces unnecessary indirection layers (_create_block_reference, _get_undefined, _render_block, _async_render_block) without addressing the fundamental design problem. Context now has rendering responsibilities mixed with its core data management role. The helper methods are thin wrappers that don't add meaningful abstraction, and duplicating sync/async logic in Context increases maintenance burden.

code_quality.justification: Code is readable with appropriate docstrings, but introduces unnecessary complexity. The _create_block_reference and _get_undefined methods are trivial wrappers with no real value. The _render_block and _async_render_block methods duplicate the exact same feature envy pattern (accessing eval_ctx.output_coerce_mode and environment.get_block_output_processor), just in a different class. Names are reasonable but don't justify the added indirection.

method_placement.justification: Methods are moved from BlockReference to Context, but this doesn't represent moving to 'the class that owns the data.' Context still accesses data from eval_ctx and environment. The placement is arguably worse since Context is now mixing data management with rendering logic. The original simple pattern in BlockReference would have been more appropriate than this relocation.

data_locality_and_delegation.justification: Data locality is not improved. The _render_block and _async_render_block methods still access self.eval_ctx.output_coerce_mode (foreign data from EvalContext) and self.environment.get_block_output_processor (delegating to Environment which then delegates to utils). The same multi-dot navigation and foreign data access exists, just in Context instead of BlockReference. Delegation hides coupling without fixing it.

object_navigation_and_law_of_demeter.justification: Law of Demeter violations persist unchanged, just relocated to Context._render_block. The code still uses self.eval_ctx.output_coerce_mode (two-level navigation) and self.environment.get_block_output_processor (accessing Environment's pass-through method). BlockReference now calls self._context._render_block(), which internally performs the same problematic navigation. The smell is moved, not eliminated.

responsibility_allocation_and_cohesion.justification: Responsibility allocation worsens. Context now has rendering responsibilities (_render_block, _async_render_block) mixed with its core data management role, reducing cohesion. The output processing logic is still fragmented—EvalContext provides the mode, Environment provides the processor, and Context makes the decisions. Environment.get_block_output_processor remains as a pass-through. The fix doesn't establish clear ownership; it just adds another class to the responsibility chain.

aspect_3_judge.summary: This refactoring relocates the feature envy from BlockReference to Context without addressing the root cause. The same problematic object navigation (eval_ctx.output_coerce_mode, environment.get_block_output_processor) persists, and cross-file smell artifacts (Environment.get_block_output_processor, utils registry) remain untouched. The fix introduces unnecessary indirection layers and worsens cohesion by mixing rendering responsibilities into Context's data management role.
